purpose: The pilot slice: how Oblivion measures a frame and who consumes the measurement. Mostly known from OBVR (knowledge/frame-clock.md), so the run measures the workflow more than the engine.

functions.name: TimeInfo update (seed: OBVR)
functions.known: read (knowledge/frame-clock.md, OBVR src/game/FrameClockLogic.h): thiscall on the TimeInfo at 0x00B33E90, argument = GetTickCount of this frame, ret 4. Takes the frame's length as integer milliseconds (tick minus +0x10), a zero reads as 1, over 166.67 (float at 0x00A3D14C) reads as 166 (0xA6), stores ms*0.001*multiplier (float at 0x00B06704, fmul at 0x0047D247) into +0x0C. +0x00 frozen flag writes zero; +0x04 nonzero = iFPSClamp fixed step with its carry at +0x08. measured (OBVR 2026-10-23): 13.33 ms frames read as 13 or 14 under Proton at 75 Hz.
questions: What do the two globals 0x00B39DB0 and 0x00B39DB4 written at the top hold (this tick and the previous one?), and who reads them?
What exactly happens on the iFPSClamp path (+0x04 nonzero): how is the carry at +0x08 used?
What does the negative-delta path (iVar3 < 0, the add of 0x00A2FC78) compute?

functions.name: update step (seed: OBVR)
functions.known: read (OBVR GameAddresses.h:811, docs/vr-modding/engine-behavior.md:142): the per-frame update step with fourteen IsMenuMode calls gating Havok pause (0x0040D809), animations (0x0040DB5B), sound (0x0040DBAB), actors (0x0040DBFB), physics step (0x0040DE3F), weather (0x0040DE76); calls GetTickCount around 0x0040D89F and the TimeInfo update at 0x0040D8AB. Ghidra's analysis had no function here; it was created from the OBVR entry (tools/ghidra/CreateFunction.java), so the body range is Ghidra's guess after that.
questions: Which systems are advanced by this function in which order, and which read TimeInfo.frameSeconds?
Is the TimeInfo update the only clock source in the step, or is GetTickCount read elsewhere in it too?
